dedupe_keys.name: hrsa nchwa health workforce projections us supply and demand of healthcare occupations by state 2023 2038 health workforce simulation model

description: This table projects how many doctors, nurses, paramedics, therapists and other health workers the United States will have, and how many it will need, every year from 2023 to 2038, nationally and state by state. The producer is the National Center for Health Workforce Analysis at the Health Resources and Services Administration, which runs the Health Workforce Simulation Model, a microsimulation of new entrants, retirements, hours worked and population demand for care. Coverage spans well over a hundred occupations in seven groups, from physician specialties and registered nurses to emergency medical technicians and long-term care aides, with metro and non-metro splits for several groups. Each row gives full-time-equivalent supply and demand, percent adequacy, and alternative scenarios for fewer or more graduates, earlier or later retirement, and wider insurance, improved access or elevated need. The full workbook is available as a free download from the HRSA data warehouse, alongside an interactive dashboard, and the data are declared public domain. Caveats: base-year supply and demand are assumed roughly balanced for many occupations, some inputs come from the pandemic period, and values are rounded to the nearest ten. Simulation uses: setting staffing limits in hospital and emergency service capacity models and testing future surge capability. Related records: the WHO health infrastructure indicators (data-who-gho-health-infrastructure-indicators) give an international view of workforce density.

schema_summary: One stacked table (sheet 'Stacked FY2025', about 102,500 rows): year, profession group, profession and definitions, state, rurality (metro or non-metro), region; full-time-equivalent supply under status quo and fewer graduates, more graduates, retire early and retire late scenarios; demand under status quo and urban, insurance, race, income, improved access, unmet need and elevated need scenarios; percent adequacy (supply divided by demand); values rounded to the nearest ten

sources.note: Workforce Projections page: NCHWA projections of the future supply of and demand for healthcare occupations at state and national level, by discipline, with 'What if?' scenarios; some data from the pandemic period; data as of 12/18/2025; dashboard data file Workforce Projections XLSX (5.0 MB)

Projections from the Health Workforce Simulation Model (HWSM), an integrated microsimulation of supply and demand by occupation, area and year; occupational groups All Health Workforce, Allied Health (including Emergency Medical Technicians and Paramedics), Behavioral Health, Long-Term Care, Oral Health, Primary Care, Women's Health; years 2023-2038; supply scenarios fewer or more graduates (10 percent) and retire early or late (two years); state data for selected occupations; 'All data from this dashboard are in the public domain and can be used freely'
